faqs.a: EMI means Equated Monthly Instalment. It is the fixed amount you pay every month to repay a loan. Each EMI has two parts: one pays down your loan amount (principal) and the other pays the lender's interest.

Three honest levers: borrow less (bigger down payment), choose a shorter tenure, or find a lower interest rate. Prepaying a lump sum early in the tenure cuts interest the most, because interest is charged on the remaining balance.
faqs.q: How can I reduce my EMI or my interest?

faqs.a: Because interest is charged on the outstanding balance. In the beginning the balance is at its highest, so most of your payment goes to interest. As the balance shrinks, a bigger share of each EMI goes toward the principal. This shift is called amortisation.
faqs.q: Why does my early EMI pay mostly interest?

faqs.a: A longer tenure lowers your monthly EMI but raises the total interest a lot. If you can afford the higher monthly payment, a shorter tenure saves you serious money. Use the tenure slider above and watch the total interest change.
faqs.q: Should I pick a longer tenure for a smaller EMI?

faqs.a: Yes, especially early on. Since interest is charged on what you still owe, paying extra in the first few years removes the most expensive part of the loan. Even one extra EMI per year can shave months or years off a long loan.

No. The flat rate looks smaller because it is calculated on the original loan amount for the whole tenure. The reducing-balance rate is charged only on what you still owe. Always compare loans on the reducing-balance rate, which is what this calculator uses.
faqs.q: Is the lender's flat rate the same as the reducing-balance rate?

emi-calculator.formula:
EMI = P x r x (1 + r)^n / ((1 + r)^n - 1)
P = loan amount, r = monthly rate (annual rate / 12 / 100), n = total months.
With 0% interest, EMI = P / n.
howTo: Enter the loan amount (principal), for example Rs. 5,00,000.
Enter the annual interest rate exactly as the lender quotes it, for example 9%.
Choose the loan tenure in years.
See your EMI, total interest, and total payable instantly.
Try a shorter tenure or a bigger down payment and watch how much interest you save.
keyFacts: EMI means Equated Monthly Instalment - a fixed monthly payment that covers both principal and interest.
Early EMIs pay mostly interest, while later EMIs pay mostly principal. This gradual shift is called amortisation.
This calculator uses monthly compounding at the monthly interest rate (annual rate / 12).
On floating-rate loans, the lender can change your EMI or your tenure when rates are revised.
Processing fees, insurance, and GST are not included. Ask your lender for the full cost.
Prepayments cut interest the most when they are made early in the loan tenure.
